summary: October retail sales grew just 0.4% and home prices fell again, as a robot factory shows China's push to mass-produce humanoids and the US closes a route to AI chips.
body: China's shoppers are still cautious. Official figures show retail sales rose only 0.4% in October from a year earlier, down from 1.1% in September and below forecasts, even with a week-long national holiday.[^1][^6] Factory output grew 4.8%, and investment in things like buildings and equipment fell 8.1% in the first ten months.[^1][^6] The statistics bureau said "the imbalance between strong supply and weak demand persists".[^1] Chinese state media says the consumer market is still expanding, pointing to faster growth in spending on services, and a bureau spokesperson said people's ability and willingness to spend need to be strengthened.[^2]

Housing, where most Chinese families keep their savings, is still sliding. New home prices fell 0.1% in October and 2.4% from a year earlier, the slowest yearly drop in almost a year.[^3] Shanghai was the only big city where prices rose, and an analyst told Reuters that ready-built homes buyers can "see and touch" have become prized after years of unfinished projects.[^3]

In Foshan, near Shenzhen, CNN got rare access to a Leju Robotics factory that aims to build up to 10,000 humanoid robots a year for factories and other jobs.[^4] Its engineering director said the hard part is not building one robot but building 10,000 to the same standard.[^4] Meanwhile, the US says that from Nov 19, firms in five countries including Singapore and Malaysia will need licences for advanced AI chips, to stop Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres abroad.[^5]
differences: The statistics bureau and state media stress stability and growth in services; foreign wire reports and analysts focus on weak spending and a property slump with "little indication of price recovery".[^1][^2][^3]

reads.title: Inside the Chinese factory building humanoid robots for the world
reads.summary: A rare look inside a humanoid robot factory in Foshan: how the machines are built and tested, and why making thousands is harder than making one.
